title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "You can draft the studs, but you gotta START the studs. Ask the fella who left forty on the pine."
tagline: Week 3 — The Recap Nobody Asked For
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Grab a seat in the film room, folks, because Week 3 was a study in margins. One matchup came down to less than half a point, one running back went for forty all by his lonesome, and three starting defenses got together and decided to score absolutely nothing. The Lambs are the last unbeaten standing, one 'Dream Team' finally found a pulse, and Cracked Out Uncle discovered a fresh, cruel way to lose. Chalk's in my hand. Let's roll it.

matchups.recap: The mascot came to play. Brock Bowers (27.6) was a monster at tight end, CeeDee Lamb (20.2) kept humming, and a 19.0 from the Vikings D/ST plus a clean 18.94 from Dak Prescott made this a wire-to-wire beatdown — even with Tetairoa McMillan (3.7) laying an egg in the starting lineup. Bang average got a huge George Kittle line (26.2) and 21.3 from Kenneth Walker III, but Jaylen Waddle (6.4) and T.J. Hockenson (3.1) out of the flex gave them almost nothing.
matchups.trashTalk: Bang average was banged below average this week — Kittle carried the barn and everybody else clocked out early. Major Tuddy dropped 153 and the mascot outscored half that lineup. Woof.

matchups.recap: Balanced and mean. Harold Fannin Jr. (24.1) went off at tight end, Lamar Jackson (20.44) did Lamar things, and Javonte Williams (18.3) and Bhayshul Tuten (17.0) gave the Panthers a real spine. Champ started Josh Allen (17.46) and got 21.8 from Kyren Williams, but Justin Jefferson (5.2) whiffed, Jalen Coker (3.8) gave nothing out of the flex-ish spot, and Dalton Schultz (6.0) couldn't chip in enough to keep pace.
matchups.trashTalk: Champ 🏆 wore the crown and scored a league-low 108 — that trophy's looking more like a participation ribbon. Mauled by the Panthers clawed off a defense that didn't matter and still cruised. Some Champ.

matchups.recap: The nail-biter of the week — 0.48 points, the whole ballgame. Ja'Marr Chase (24.8), Derrick Henry (21.9), and Davante Adams (20.7) did the heavy lifting for the still-perfect Lambs, who won DESPITE a 0.0 from the Patriots D/ST. Cracked Out Uncle got a monster from Drake London (28.4) and 21.0 from Tee Higgins, but the 49ers D/ST laid a 0.0 goose egg AND Jaylen Warren (20.6) and Michael Wilson (25.9) — a combined 46.5 — sat on the bench in a game lost by less than half a point.
matchups.trashTalk: Silence of the CeeDee Lambs stayed silent, stayed perfect, and stole one by a hair. Cracked Out Uncle, my guy — you left 46 points on the bench and lost by 0.48. That's not snakebitten anymore, that's a curse with a lease.

matchups.recap: The dream finally got some sleep. Jahmyr Gibbs (41.4) detonated for a league-high, and Chris Olave (19.7), Deebo Samuel (15.4), and a tidy 12.0 from the kicker gave the Dream Team its supporting cast at last — even with a 0.0 from the Bengals D/ST. Questionable or Kicked rode Jaxon Smith-Njigba (35.36) and Sam Darnold (27.66), and correctly started Darnold over the benched Joe Burrow (22.58) in this one-QB league, but Dalton Kincaid (3.8) and Steelers D/ST (4.0) couldn't keep pace.
matchups.trashTalk: Kelce's Wildest Dream Team spent two weeks as a nightmare and finally found the supporting cast — turns out Gibbs going for forty will do that. Questionable or Kicked got a rocket from JSN again and STILL got outgunned. First loss stings, front-runner.

matchups.recap: Hope turned real for a week. Garrett Wilson (26.7) and Christian Watson (22.6) went off, McCaffrey (21.6) was steady, and a 16.0 from kicker Harrison Mevis proved the difference in a shootout. AllInTheTush had its own fireworks — Bijan Robinson (35.3) and Brock Purdy (31.28) were electric and Jeremiyah Love (21.9) chipped in — but De'Von Achane (1.7), Chris Godwin (5.5), and Omarion Hampton (5.6) sank the ship.
matchups.trashTalk: False Hope, would you look at that — after a week-low disaster you dropped 148 and lived up to the good half of the name. AllInTheTush got 66 from Bijan and Purdy alone and STILL lost; when the flex and the RB2 no-show, that's AllInTheLoss.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: A league-high detonation that finally made the Dream Team a dream.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: Ground it out all day in a shootout win.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: A started RB with a projection near 20 that gave almost nothing — in a 6-point loss.

awards.label: Bench Blunder
awards.note: Benched Wilson (25.9) AND Warren (20.6) — 46.5 combined — while the 49ers D/ST posted 0.0. Lost by 0.48.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.note: Three started defenses combined for a fat zero. The Uncle's goose egg was the one that cost a game.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: A tight end nobody drafted turning in a stud line.

momentOfWeek.text: Cracked Out Uncle losing by 0.48 points — with a 0.0 from his starting D/ST and Michael Wilson (25.9) and Jaylen Warren (20.6) stapled to the bench for a combined 46.5. Any one of them off the pine and the Uncle wins going away. Instead he's 0-3 and the ghost of Week 1's 51.5-point benching is now officially haunting this franchise. Set. Your. Lineup.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: Only 3-0 team in the league — wins ugly, wins anyway. Scary.
Balanced and bruising. Handed the Champ a season low.
Week-high 153. The mascot is officially a problem.
JSN keeps flying but the front-runner tasted its first L.
148 and a win — the name's only half true this week.
Gibbs went for 40 and the cast finally showed. Dream's alive.
Bijan and Purdy dropped 66 and it wasn't enough. Snakebit.
Kittle solo act. The rest was, well, below average.
Left 46 on the bench, lost by 0.48, fell to 0-3. Cursed.

lastWord: That's Week 3, gang. We learned Gibbs can win a week by himself, three defenses can all score nothing on the same Sunday, and you can score 133 and STILL fall to 0-3 if the points you need are watching from the bench. The Lambs are perfect, the Uncle is snakebitten beyond belief, and the fastest way to the film room is leaving your studs stapled to the pine. Set your lineups, trust your studs, and Cracked Out Uncle — for the love of the game, START THE GUYS WHO SCORE. Reinebold out.
